title: Sharkey Bonano, Freddie and Bunk, and the district joints
summary: Keppard talks about Sharky's cornet, Freddie's fear of Bunk's Maple Leaf Rag, then playing in Storyville places on Custom House and Basin Streets.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, he's all right, but he doesn't have much depth anymore.

He's kind of tired out. Well, yeah. Well, you see, Sharky used to be a tough man. I believe he was Italian, Mr. Roussel. I think so. He was a little short, skinny man. But they tell me he didn't got stout. I ain't seen him so long.
Well, yeah, he's still a little small. He's pretty short, but he's got a stomach.

Yeah. Well, I must give him what's coming to him. He had a good lift. He did. If I'm mistaken, I believe Mal Flores showed him. If I'm mistaken, I believe it is. Mal Flores showed him. And, of course, he came out to be good. He's one out of 100. My brother used to say, you know something between him and Bunk, I don't know which one I'm scared of. He said, all right. He said, because Bunk plays that maple leaf rag with such a nice tone, and it comes out, and he figured that corner's so good, he said, this fellow on the lake there, you can hear him cross the water. He used to tell my mother all the time. He said, you know, I don't know who is the best, but I'm scared of all of them. When we used to get on the advertising, Fred was scared of getting out there, because he knew right well Bunk will put that maple leaf rag on him, and he knew right well Bunk was a nice thing in corner, as you know it yourself, Mr. Rosario. In his days. You know, of course, the poor fellow, I'm sorry for him, but God knows the best. He had to die, so like all the rest of us, but you see, and during the district time, when I got away from that jury store, I went and played at Hans, and they had this fellow, Josh Jones, on Basin Street, Cornelius, they was playing at Tom Anderson. Of course, now don't get me wrong, it wasn't Iverville Street, no, it was Custom House Street. Custom House, yes. It was Custom, or Custom House Street, and now it's Iverville. That's because I said, I don't want to say Iverville now, because I know it was Custom House Street that time. They never had no pavement out there on the street. They had nothing but the old gutters and other things, and a little white, and Mel Bryant, and Frantz Alambritz, and May Tucker, oh, I know this way they was, all through that Iverville Street. Tom Anderson was on Basin and Beville, Barry Basin and Iverville, and they had the maestrian, he was on the other side of Rapport Street. Well, I believe this one, he used to play over there. What's the name again? Peter Roy used to play over there, and that's that,
